title: Invertibility of the canonical mate for integral quotient reduction
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, schemes $X,Y$, a morphism $f:X\to Y$, Chern data $c_Y,c_X$ [def-sp-tower-class-chern], and intermediate coefficient pullback data $d$ [def-sp-tower-chern-pullback-intermediate]. Let $L_T\dashv U_T^D$ be the recorded derived reduction adjunctions [def-sp-tower-class-reduction], $F$ the exact inverse image of abelian towers [lem-sp-tower-integral-class-pullback], $P=d.\mathrm{pull}$, and $b:U_Y^D F^D\simeq P^D U_X^D$ the localization of $d.\mathrm{forgetIso}$. Define $\lambda:F^D L_X\to L_Y P^D$ to be the adjunction mate of $b$, characterized by $\eta_X(F^D M)\,U_X^D(\lambda_M)=F^D(\eta_Y(M))\,b_{L_Y M}$. Then $\lambda$ is invertible. No normalization of the integer or root comparisons is assumed, and no such endpoint equation is concluded. Compositions are left to right.

proof.text: Realize integer towers and quotient module systems on the sequence site. The section-normalized forgetful square identifies the given module inverse image with geometric inverse image: at each level the normalized constant Z/ell^(n+1) action is unique, and all maps of the underlying torsion sheaves are linear. Retain the actual quotient transitions.

proof.text: Transport this comparison to the specified reduction functors using their universal derived counits. Their representative transpose equations identify its inverse as the canonical adjunction mate: its transpose is inverse image of the source adjunction unit followed by the derived forgetful square. Equality on representatives extends by localization, and injectivity of the target hom equivalence identifies the components. Hence the specified mate is invertible.
